reading.title: Linguistic Relativity and Language Structure
reading.passage: The Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, a foundational concept in linguistics, proposes that language structure fundamentally shapes cognitive processes and worldview perception. This theory suggests that speakers of different languages conceptualize reality through distinct linguistic frameworks, implying that cognitive categories are not universal but rather linguistically determined. For instance, languages with multiple grammatical aspects for expressing time may cultivate different temporal perspectives among speakers compared to languages with minimal temporal distinctions. Empirical research has provided nuanced support for this hypothesis, demonstrating moderate correlations between linguistic features and cognitive patterns. While strong versions of linguistic determinism have been largely refuted, contemporary scholars acknowledge that language exerts subtle but measurable influences on perception, memory, and categorization processes. The debate remains vigorous, with neuroscientific evidence increasingly revealing how linguistic properties modulate neural activation patterns during conceptual processing. This ongoing investigation underscores the intricate relationship between linguistic structure and human cognition, challenging the notion that language merely reflects pre-existing thought.

questions.q: According to the passage, what does the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis primarily claim?
options: Language is a universal system that all humans share equally.
Language structure shapes how speakers perceive and conceptualize reality.
Cognitive processes are entirely independent of linguistic influences.
Different languages have identical grammatical structures for expressing time.
questions.explanation: 지문의 첫 문장에서 언어 구조가 인지 과정과 세계관을 형성한다는 것이 가설의 핵심 주장입니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred from the passage about strong versions of linguistic determinism?
options: They remain widely accepted in modern linguistics.
They have been largely rejected based on evidence.
They are supported by all contemporary neuroscientific studies.
They explain why all languages are structurally identical.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'strong versions of linguistic determinism have been largely refuted'라고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: The word 'modulate' in the final paragraph is closest in meaning to

regulate or adjust
eliminate completely

questions.explanation: modulate는 '조절하다' 또는 '변화시키다'라는 의미로, 이 문맥에서 언어가 신경 활성화를 어떻게 조절하는지에 대해 말하고 있습니다.

questions.q: Why does the author provide the example about grammatical aspects of time?
options: To prove that all languages are completely different
To illustrate how linguistic features may influence cognitive perception
To demonstrate that time cannot be expressed in language
To argue that the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis is entirely invalid

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer online shopping for its convenience and variety. Others prefer shopping in physical stores for the personal experience. Which do you prefer and why? Include specific reasons and details.
model_sentences: I personally prefer shopping in physical stores because I can see and touch products before buying them.
First, physically visiting a store allows me to check the quality and size immediately, which reduces the risk of ordering the wrong item.
For example, when I buy clothes, I can try them on to make sure they fit perfectly, unlike online shopping where I might have to return items multiple times.
Additionally, I enjoy the in-store experience of browsing around and discovering products I didn't plan to buy, which makes shopping more enjoyable and interactive.
Overall, while online shopping is convenient, the ability to inspect products and have a personal shopping experience makes physical stores my preferred choice.

listening.title: Dormitory Room Assignment Inquiry
listening.script:
Student: Hi, I wanted to ask about my dorm room assignment. I haven't received my housing letter yet, and I'm getting worried.
Housing Officer: Oh, I understand your concern. Let me check our system. Can you provide your student ID number?
Student: Sure, it's 2847569.
Housing Officer: One moment... Ah yes, I see your file. Your assignment has been processed, but there was a slight delay in mailing. You should receive your letter within the next two to three days.
Student: Great! But I was also wondering if it's possible to request a specific dorm or roommate.
Housing Officer: Well, the initial assignments are based on your preferences from the housing application, but if you have special circumstances, you can submit a housing change request after you move in. We typically allow changes during the first two weeks of the semester.
Student: That sounds reasonable. And when should I plan to arrive for move-in day?
Housing Officer: Move-in begins on August 25th and continues through August 30th. We recommend arriving earlier rather than later to have more parking availability. Here's a pamphlet with all the details.

questions.q: What is the main reason the student visits the housing officer?
options: To complain about the quality of dormitory facilities
To inquire about the status of their room assignment
To request a transfer to a different university
To pay the dormitory deposit fee

options: It has already been delivered to their home.

questions.q: When can students request a housing change if they want to switch rooms?
